subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class multi-index memorySearch config/storage/query routing for embedding failover now, and what API, migration, and status contract should that expose?
rationale: The request is technically plausible but crosses new config surface, SQLite schema ownership, provider failover semantics, and operator observability; automation should not pick that product/API shape.

options.title: Design contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker, approve the multi-index config/schema/status contract, then split implementation into reviewed migration and runtime PRs.

options.title: Fix narrow fallback bugs first
options.body: Defer multi-index storage and prioritize the bounded recovery bug in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96534 while keeping this feature unimplemented.

options.title: Decline broad config surface
options.body: Reject first-class multi-index config for now and require users to rebuild or use FTS-only degradation when embedding providers change.

recommendation.title: Design contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker, approve the multi-index config/schema/status contract, then split implementation into reviewed migration and runtime PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the live assignee and has recent commits in provider-failure and memory embedding behavior.
